subject: PSHE & RSE
source: National Curriculum / statutory RSHE guidance (Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education, Health Education); PSHE Association programme of study themes and KS3 mental health lessons (Drive PSHE folder); TGA RSHE Policy 2026-27, Careers Education and Guidance Policy and RECIPE Character Framework 2026-27 (Drive); existing TGA PSHE Y5 lesson style. Qur'an and hadith references limited to well-known authenticated sources and cited plainly.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Next steps and financial capability
lessons.title: Post-16 pathways: choosing and applying
objectives: Compare post-16 routes: A levels, T levels, college courses and apprenticeships
Identify entry requirements and application deadlines and make a plan with a back-up
Use reflection, consultation and istikhara alongside research to decide

keywords.def: a two-year academic qualification taken after GCSEs
a technical qualification with a substantial industry placement
paid work combined with training
grades and subjects needed for a course
the prayer for seeking guidance in a decision

teach.heading: The big picture at 16
bullets: In England you stay in education or training until 18
Routes: sixth form, college, apprenticeship, work with training
Choices are not final; routes can change
TGA Careers Lead can advise
teach.note: Say bismillah. Refer to the TGA Careers Education and Guidance Policy. TGA pupils live in different countries; use England as the baseline and encourage pupils abroad to research their local equivalents and discuss the options with the Careers Lead. Cite plainly: Qur'an 65:2-3, that whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make a way out and provide from where they do not expect. Link to RECIPE Progress. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Anonymous questions can go to the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: The main routes
bullets: A levels: academic, usually three subjects
T levels: technical, with a 45-day industry placement
Apprenticeships: earn and learn, to degree level
Applied courses (e.g. BTEC): practical, career-focused
teach.note: Explain each route with an invented pupil: Hamza wants to study medicine, so chooses A levels in Chemistry, Biology and Maths; Maryam enjoys design and chooses a T level in Digital Production; Ibrahim prefers hands-on learning and chooses an engineering apprenticeship. Discuss pros and cons. Mention that T levels and apprenticeships can lead to higher education too. Misconception: apprenticeships are a lower-status route. They lead to recognised qualifications and careers.

teach.heading: Entry requirements and research
bullets: Check grades, subjects and deadlines
Compare providers: results, location, support
Attend open days and online events
Use National Careers Service and gov.uk
teach.note: Show how to read a prospectus: entry requirements such as 5 GCSEs at grade 4 or above including English and maths, and higher grades for specific subjects. Emphasise that deadlines vary and many open in autumn. Ask pupils to create a table of three providers and compare. Remind pupils that online reviews and social media are not enough. Link to RECIPE Excellence.

teach.heading: Applications and back-up plans
bullets: Personal statement: skills, achievements, motivation
Reference from teachers
Apply to more than one option
Plan B: other courses, resits, alternative routes
teach.note: Give a personal statement structure: why this course, evidence of skills, wider activities, future goals. Worked example sentence: ‘Volunteering at a food bank taught me teamwork and reliability.’ Encourage pupils to apply for a main choice and one or two back-ups. Remind pupils that GCSE results are used by providers; resilience matters. Link to RECIPE Resilience.

teach.heading: Making the decision with guidance
bullets: Consult family, teachers and the Careers Lead
Consider your values, strengths and interests
Make istikhara and then act with trust
Do your best, then trust Allah
teach.note: Cite plainly: the Prophet (peace be upon him) taught the companions to seek guidance (istikhara) in all matters, as narrated in Bukhari. Explain that istikhara does not replace research and consultation (shura). Cite Qur'an 3:159: when you have decided, put your trust in Allah. Close with a reminder that the Careers Lead can arrange one-to-one meetings.

practice: Match the route to the description: (a) earn while learning (b) academic, three subjects (c) technical with 45-day placement.
A course needs five GCSEs at grade 4 including English and maths. Pupil A has 4s in English and maths and 5s in three other subjects. Does she meet the requirement?
List three questions you would ask at an open day.
independent: Complete a comparison table of three post-16 options with entry requirements, course content and deadlines.
Draft the opening paragraph of a personal statement for your preferred course.
Write a plan B for your first-choice route.
exit: Why is it important to have a back-up plan?
lessons.homework: Book or attend one open day or online event and write five sentences about what you learned.
lessons.send: SEND: provide a comparison table template and sentence starters. EAL: pre-teach pathways vocabulary with images. Stretch: research degree apprenticeships and compare them with a traditional degree.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Next steps and financial capability
lessons.title: Money: payslips, tax and borrowing
objectives: Calculate take-home pay from a gross salary using income tax and National Insurance
Explain how interest, APR and debt work
Describe riba and halal alternatives and make informed financial decisions

keywords.def: pay before deductions
pay after tax and other deductions
a contribution from earnings that funds state benefits
the yearly cost of borrowing as a percentage
interest or increase on a loan, forbidden in Islam

starter: Name two signs of a scam.
What is the difference between income and expenditure?

teach.heading: From gross pay to take-home pay
bullets: Gross pay: before deductions
Income tax and National Insurance are deducted
Net pay: what you take home
Pension contributions may also be taken
teach.note: Say bismillah. Show a simplified payslip. Explain that tax pays for public services. Use 2026-27 rates in England: personal allowance £12,570; basic rate 20% on income above this up to £50,270; employee National Insurance of 8% on earnings between £12,570 and £50,270 (teachers should check gov.uk for any changes). Link to RECIPE Integrity: honesty in paying what is due. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Anonymous questions can go to the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Worked example: £20,000 a year
bullets: Income tax at 20%: £1,486
National Insurance at 8%: £594.40
Net pay: £17,919.60 a year
teach.note: Walk through the calculation step by step: 7,430 × 0.20 = 1,486; 7,430 × 0.08 = 594.40; 20,000 − 1,486 − 594.40 = 17,919.60. Divide by 12 for about £1,493.30 a month. Pupils should use calculators. Misconception: tax is taken on the whole salary at 20%; only income above the allowance is taxed. Check understanding with a second example in practice.

teach.heading: Borrowing and interest
bullets: Credit cards, loans, overdrafts, buy-now-pay-later
Interest increases what you repay
APR: compare the true yearly cost
Missed payments harm your credit score
teach.note: Worked example: borrowing £1,000 at 20% APR for one year costs about £200 extra. If only minimum payments are made the cost can rise quickly. Explain credit scores and why they matter for renting and loans. Cite plainly: Qur'an 2:282, which tells believers to write down debts with a fixed term. Link to the hadith that the soul of a believer is held back by their debt until it is paid (Tirmidhi).

teach.heading: Riba and halal alternatives
bullets: Qur'an 2:275: trade is lawful, riba is forbidden
Interest-based loans are riba
Islamic finance: profit-sharing, cost-plus sale, leasing
Seek advice from qualified scholars
teach.note: Cite plainly: Qur'an 2:275-279 on riba. Explain simply how some Islamic products work: a bank buys an item and sells it at an agreed higher price (murabaha); partners share profit and loss (musharakah, mudarabah); leasing (ijara). Note that scholars discuss specific products such as student finance and mortgages; encourage pupils to consult family and qualified scholars for personal decisions. Present facts without judgement.

teach.heading: Spending wisely
bullets: Needs before wants
Save a little regularly
Give sadaqah
Hadith: asked about wealth, how earned and spent
teach.note: Cite plainly: the hadith that a person will be asked about their wealth, how it was earned and how it was spent (Tirmidhi); and Qur'an 25:67 on moderation. Discuss priorities: rent, food, transport, savings, giving. Ask: ‘What would you cut if income fell by 10%?’ Mention free sources of guidance: MoneyHelper (gov.uk). Link to RECIPE Contentment.

practice: Calculate net pay for a salary of £24,000: tax at 20% and NI at 8% on the amount above £12,570.
You borrow £500 at 24% APR for a year. Approximately how much interest is charged?
Explain the difference between gross and net pay.
independent: Create a monthly budget for someone earning £1,600 net in their first job, including rent, food, transport, savings and sadaqah.
Write a leaflet: ‘Borrowing: what to know before you sign’.
Write a paragraph explaining how Islamic finance differs from interest-based borrowing.
exit: What is the difference between gross and net pay?
Name one halal alternative to an interest-based loan.
lessons.homework: Calculate the take-home pay for a job offering £18,000 a year and write one decision you would make with the money.
lessons.send: SEND: provide a step-by-step calculation template and allow a calculator. EAL: pre-teach finance vocabulary. Stretch: compare the total repaid on a £5,000 loan at 8% and 15% APR over three years.

lessons.title: First aid: CPR, choking and severe bleeding
objectives: State the steps for responding to an unresponsive adult who is not breathing normally
Describe how to help a person who is choking and how to treat severe bleeding
Explain the recovery position and when to call 999

keywords.def: cardiopulmonary resuscitation: chest compressions to keep blood moving
a device that gives an electric shock to restart a normal heart rhythm
a side-lying position that keeps the airway clear
the passage that carries air to the lungs
the UK emergency number

starter: Bismillah. What number do you call in an emergency?
Name two parts of the body that need oxygen.
Why is it important to stay calm?

teach.heading: Why first aid matters
bullets: Quick action can save lives
Anyone can learn the basics
Check for danger first
Qur'an 5:32: saving one life is like saving all mankind
teach.note: Say bismillah. Cite plainly: Qur'an 5:32, that whoever saves a life it is as if they saved all of humanity. Emphasise that this lesson does not replace an accredited course such as St John Ambulance or Red Cross; encourage pupils to take one. Pupils practise on a cushion or pillow only; no pupil touches another. TGA pupils may live in different countries: use 999 for the UK and tell pupils to learn their local emergency number. Link to RECIPE Excellence. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Anonymous questions can go to the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: CPR: DR ABC
bullets: Danger: is it safe?
Response: shake shoulders, shout
Airway and Breathing: tilt head, look for normal breathing
Call 999, start CPR
teach.note: Teach the sequence. If the person does not respond and is not breathing normally, call 999 (put on speaker), ask for an ambulance and a defibrillator. Compressions: heel of hand on the centre of the chest, press down 5 to 6 cm, 100 to 120 per minute, about the tempo of ‘Stayin’ Alive’. If trained and willing, give 2 rescue breaths after every 30 compressions; otherwise do hands-only CPR. Practise for one minute on a cushion with a metronome or music.

teach.heading: Defibrillators (AED)
bullets: Public AEDs give clear voice instructions
Switch on and follow the prompts
Attach pads as shown
Anyone can use one safely
teach.note: Explain that an AED analyses the heart rhythm and only gives a shock if needed. Pads are placed on bare chest as shown on the pads. Do not touch the person during analysis. Continue CPR until help arrives or the person breathes normally. Mention that many public places have AEDs and the 999 call handler can help locate one.

teach.heading: Choking and severe bleeding
bullets: Choking: encourage coughing first
5 back blows between shoulder blades
5 abdominal thrusts if still blocked; call 999
Bleeding: press firmly with a clean pad and call 999
teach.note: Teach choking for adults and children over one: if they cannot cough, speak or breathe, give up to 5 back blows, then up to 5 abdominal thrusts, alternating; call 999 if not cleared. For severe bleeding: apply firm direct pressure with a clean cloth, do not remove objects stuck in the wound, keep pressing, add more padding if soaked, call 999. Wash hands afterwards. Note that these are summary steps; direct pupils to the St John Ambulance website.

teach.heading: Recovery position and staying safe
bullets: Breathing normally but unresponsive: place on their side
Keep checking breathing
Stay with them until help arrives
Look after your own safety and wellbeing
teach.note: Describe the recovery position: kneel beside the person, place the nearest arm at a right angle, place the other hand against their cheek, bend the far knee and roll them towards you, tilt the head back to keep the airway open. Practise with a cushion or described steps. Discuss emotions after an emergency; it is normal to feel shaken; talk to someone. Close with a du'a for those in need.

practice: Put in order: (a) call 999 (b) check for danger (c) check response (d) start chest compressions (e) check breathing.
How deep and how fast should adult chest compressions be?
What are two actions you would take if someone has a severe bleed?
independent: Make a step-by-step poster: ‘What to do if someone collapses’.
Practise CPR on a cushion for two minutes and record how you kept the pace.
Write a paragraph on why learning first aid is part of caring for others in Islam.
exit: What number would you call in the UK for an emergency?
lessons.homework: Watch a St John Ambulance or Red Cross first aid video with a parent, then teach one skill to a family member.
lessons.send: SEND: provide a visual CPR flowchart and allow practice without time pressure. EAL: pre-teach first aid vocabulary with images. Stretch: research how to treat burns or fractures and create a quick-reference card.

lessons.title: Sexual health, consent and the law: facts for safe, informed choices
objectives: Explain consent and the law, including the age of consent and sexual harassment
Describe, in factual terms, sexual health risks and where to find confidential NHS support
Link Islamic teaching on modesty, marriage and responsibility to making informed choices

keywords.def: freely given agreement that can be withdrawn at any time
an infection that can pass on through sexual contact
unwanted sexual behaviour that makes someone feel uncomfortable or unsafe
choosing not to have sexual relationships
being accountable for your choices and their effects

starter: Name two people or services you can ask for help.

teach.heading: Setting the scene
bullets: Factual health education for 15 and 16-year-olds
Taught within the TGA RSHE Policy
Parents have been informed
Questions go to the anonymous question box
teach.note: Say bismillah. Teacher note: this lesson is statutory Health Education and Relationships Education content at KS4, taught factually and sensitively in line with the TGA RSHE Policy and in line with Islamic ethos. Parents have been informed and shown the resources. Pupils need to know the facts to keep themselves safe whatever choices they make in life. Follow the policy on any parental withdrawal request for sex education. Take questions through the box only. Ground rules are essential. Link to RECIPE Integrity and amanah. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Anonymous questions can go to the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Consent and the law
bullets: Consent must be free, informed and can be withdrawn
The age of consent in the UK is 16
Sexual harassment and assault are crimes
Silence, pressure or being intoxicated is not consent
teach.note: Revisit consent from Y9. State the law factually: sexual activity without consent is a crime, and the age of consent is 16 in England and Wales. Explain that pressure, threats and incapacity through alcohol or drugs mean there is no consent. Explain that sexual harassment, including online, is unacceptable. If a pupil is a victim, it is never their fault. Rape Crisis: 0808 500 2222; Childline: 0800 1111.

teach.heading: Islamic teaching on relationships
bullets: Qur'an 17:32: do not go near zina
Qur'an 24:30-31: lower the gaze and guard modesty
Marriage is the context for intimacy
Qur'an 30:21: love and mercy within marriage
teach.note: Cite plainly: Qur'an 17:32 tells believers not to approach unlawful sexual intercourse; 24:30-31 on lowering the gaze and guarding chastity; and 30:21 on love and mercy within marriage. State clearly that the Islamic position is that intimate relationships belong within marriage. Teach respectfully and avoid shaming. Emphasise Allah's mercy, and that anyone who has erred can turn back in repentance. Link to RECIPE Eeman.

teach.heading: Sexual health facts
bullets: STIs can pass on through sexual contact
Some have no symptoms; many are treatable
Abstinence outside marriage is the only certain protection
NHS services are confidential and free
teach.note: Give factual, brief information: STIs such as chlamydia can have no symptoms and can be treated; HIV and hepatitis B are serious but manageable with treatment; testing is available through sexual health clinics and GPs and is confidential. The HPV vaccine is offered through schools in England. Explain that contraception exists and that the Islamic position on family planning within marriage has been discussed by scholars, including the narration about ‘azl (Bukhari and Muslim); pupils with questions should ask a parent or qualified scholar. Do not give practical instructions.

teach.heading: Where to get help
bullets: GP or NHS 111
Sexual health clinics: confidential for under 18s
Childline 0800 1111
TGA DSL and pastoral team
teach.note: Show how to find an NHS sexual health service at nhs.uk. Explain that young people under 16 can receive confidential advice and care, though a professional may need to tell someone if a young person is at risk of harm. Remind pupils that they can talk to the DSL at any time. Revisit the importance of intentions, responsibility and choosing safe paths. Close with a du'a for guidance and purity of heart.

practice: True or false? (a) Consent can be withdrawn at any time. (b) The age of consent in England and Wales is 18. (c) NHS sexual health services are confidential.
Write one sentence explaining why consent cannot be given under pressure.
Name two places a young person can go for confidential health advice.
independent: Create a fact sheet: ‘Know your rights and responsibilities’ with six facts and three services.
Write a response to a friend who says they are being pressured by someone online.
Write a paragraph explaining how Islamic teaching on modesty, marriage and responsibility supports safety and dignity.
exit: Name one confidential place to get sexual health advice.
lessons.homework: Look at the NHS website section on sexual health and write three facts you learned and one question for the PSHE Lead.
lessons.send: SEND: provide fact cards and a simple glossary; offer a private check-in. EAL: pre-teach vocabulary with simple definitions. Stretch: research the Online Safety Act 2023 and how it protects young people from harmful content.
